subject: Clarify data residency, retention & cross-border flow for FinServe POC
messages:
From: Laura King <laura.king@finserve.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarification: Data residency & cross-border transfers for FinServe POC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed with the POC, our security team has a few specific questions about where data will be processed and any cross-border transfers that might occur during the POC and later in production:

1) Which cloud regions will inference traffic and logs touch for the hosted Redwood API? Is data processed only in the customer-selected region?
2) Which subprocessors are involved (cloud providers, logging/telemetry vendors, analytics)?
3) If we route requests to a model variant hosted in another region (for capacity/burst), will data cross borders? What controls/fallbacks exist?
4) How long does Redwood retain request/response logs for POCs, and do you provide a deletion API or certificate once data is deleted?

We need concise answers and any supporting artifacts (SOC2/infra diagrams) for our procurement & security review. Copying our security alias: security@finserve.com.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we aim to kick off the POC next week.

Best,
Laura King
Head of Cloud Integrations
FinServe Inc.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Laura King <laura.king@finserve.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarification: Data residency & cross-border transfers for FinServe POC

Laura — thanks for the clear list. Answering inline to keep this tight; attaching a short summary PDF and our SCQ workbook for the POC.

1) Regions & processing:
- Hosted API: customers choose the primary region for request processing (US, EU, APAC regions available). For your POC we can pin to eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) or us-east-1 depending on your preference.
- Inference is executed in the customer-selected region by default. Metadata (billing, non-PII telemetry) may be replicated to other regions for analytics/backplane purposes but only in aggregated form unless you opt into cross-region telemetry.

2) Subprocessors (high level):
- Compute: AWS (EC2/GPU instances) and GCP (for select APAC regions) depending on capacity and region.
- Storage & object logs: AWS S3 / GCS depending on compute plane.
- Observability / metrics: Datadog (aggregated traces), Sentry (errors).
- Identity & keys: customer KMS (when configured) or Redwood-managed KMS (AWS KMS).
We can produce a full subprocessor list with endpoints for legal review — included in the attached SCQ workbook.

3) Cross-border transfers & capacity failover:
- Default behavior: Redwood routes requests to the model/variant pinned to the chosen region.
- Burst/failover: If capacity is constrained, routing policy can: (a) queue and respect region-only processing; (b) route to a compatible model in another region (cross-region transfer); or (c) fallback to a lower-tier model in the same region.
- Controls: you select the policy. For FinServe POC we recommend configuring "region-strict" — no cross-region routing allowed. For production we can set prioritized routing with explicit audit logs for any cross-region hops.

4) Retention & deletion:
- Request/response logs: default retention is 30 days for hosted accounts. For customers under contract we support configurable retention down to 0 days and can enforce deletion windows via policy.
- Deletion API & attestation: we provide a deletion API for artifacts retained by Redwood and can supply a deletion certificate/audit record (timestamped) on request. For POC work we typically set retention to 7 days unless you require otherwise.

Next steps:
- I attached Redwood_Data_Residency_Summary.pdf (high-level) and POC_SCQ_Response.xlsx with the subprocessor list and recommended settings.
- If you want region-strict for the POC, reply with your preferred region and I’ll mark the account accordingly and loop our S&C lead (Neha) for a short technical confirmation.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0104

From: Laura King <laura.king@finserve.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finserve.com
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarification: Data residency & cross-border transfers for FinServe POC

Thanks Priyom — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups from our security team:

- Can you confirm whether per-request telemetry (latency, token counts) ever contains PII or payload snippets? We prefer telemetry to be strictly metadata.
- For the deletion certificate: what fields are included (what's the format) and how soon after deletion is the certificate generated?
- Do you have SOC 2 Type II evidence we can share with procurement, or do we need to sign an NDA first?

We'd like the POC pinned to eu-west-1 (Frankfurt) and region-strict. Will that configuration require a contract addendum?

Best,
Laura

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura King <laura.king@finserve.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 09:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarification: Data residency & cross-border transfers for FinServe POC

Hi Laura — looping in quick technical clarifications from the security team. Forwarded answers below and attaching a link to the detailed infra diagram.

On telemetry content:
- Per-request telemetry is limited to operational metadata (latency, token counts, HTTP statuses). We do not capture full prompt/response payloads in telemetry unless a customer enables debug logging. If debug logging is enabled, it is opt-in and clearly called out in the account settings.

Deletion certificate details:
- Format: PDF with: deletion timestamp (UTC), object identifiers (log file names/keys), retention policy id, and a SHA256 digest of the deleted archive (for non-real-time deletions).
- Timing: For manual deletion requests we issue the certificate within 24 hours of successful deletion. For automated retention expirations the certificate is generated as part of the scheduled job and available within 48 hours.

SOC 2 / evidence:
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II; procurement can receive the SOC 2 report after an NDA. For customers with enterprise contracts we include SOC 2 review in the standard diligence package.

POC region-strict in eu-west-1:
- No contract addendum needed for a POC. We'll set the POC account to region-strict as requested; production commitments (SLA/retention below 30 days) will require the standard contract language.

Link to infra & SCQ: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/FinServe-Residency-Notes

If useful, Monica can schedule a 30 minute technical run-through with your security engineer.

— Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
